source.title: Changing the Training Data Distribution to Reduce Simplicity Bias Improves In-distribution Generalization
source.authors: Dang Nguyen; P. Haddad; E. Gan; Baharan Mirzasoleiman

record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and reports test error for image classifiers, but does not directly compare large and small batches in the text.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label generalization results and a batch-size ablation. It does not test random-label memorization or the other listed versions. Batch-size values are shown only in Figure 14.
record.test_reason: The batch-size ablation measures held-out error at a fixed 200-epoch budget, bearing on V5, although its direction cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. The architecture experiments also bear on V3: convolutional classifiers and a fully connected MLP are trained from scratch on CIFAR10 with standard gradient methods.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that SAM learns fast- and slow-learnable features more evenly than GD, and that early clustering followed by one-shot upsampling reduces simplicity bias and improves in-distribution performance with SGD or SAM, including when combined with augmentation.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the training data distribution by clustering examples early and upsampling one cluster; it does not use the claim's random-label memorization setup or compare the claim's listed optimizer, architecture, or regularization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size is varied in the CIFAR10 ablation; the text does not state its effect on test error.

fits_no_version.finding: USEFUL improves SGD and SAM test performance by upsampling examples identified early as slow-learnable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the training distribution through early targeted upsampling can improve in-distribution image classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports Hessian maximum eigenvalues of 53.8, 41.8, and 12.4 and spectral ratios of 3.8, 1.5, and 2.4 for SGD, SGD+USEFUL, and SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: USEFUL changes Hessian-based sharpness measures; these measures do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: USEFUL and SAM reduce example-forgetting scores, and slow-learnable clusters have higher forgetting scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Targeted upsampling changes example-learning dynamics; forgetting scores do not measure the memorization influence or removal intervention named in V8.

record.problems: The batch-size results are figure-only in the supplied text, with no described direction or exact values. Main experiments report averages over three seeds, but the batch-size figure's exact uncertainty values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure 14 batch-size values are represented as figure-only rows because the supplied text does not provide recoverable numbers.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fully random labels paired with natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out performance. Partial label corruption with MixUp does not test this conjunction.
A width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
The causal contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, and initialization from a trained convolutional network.
Adaptive gradient optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. SAM and ASAM comparisons do not supply this comparison.
Longer training, batch-dependent learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization changes, and language-model workloads.
Controlled dropout addition or removal, dropout-strength sweeps, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of examples selected by label-memorization influence, retraining, and comparison against equally sized random removals.

missing.what: Add matched CIFAR10 architecture-comparison rows for ordinary momentum SGD: three-layer MLP 42.59%, ResNet18 5.07%, VGG19 6.68%, and DenseNet121 10.43% test error. Record the MLP's 512-unit hidden size and dropout 0.1, plus the shared training settings and architecture-specific differences. The record incorrectly declares V3 untested.
missing.locator: Sections 5.2–5.3; Appendix C.1 and D.2; Figures 4, 5, and 9

record.verdict_notes: No V5 verdict is justified from the supplied text: Figure 14's axes survive extraction, but its plotted values and cross-batch trends do not. Its caption establishes use of standard settings, including a fixed epoch budget. The architecture comparison supports V3 in the tested recipes without isolating local connectivity as the cause.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and their initialization or connectivity variants.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD.
The text does not state the direction or magnitude of test-error changes across batch sizes; Figure 14 is the only batch-size result.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
